findings.title: Missing billing access check exposes invoices to plain members
findings.explanation: The other invoice routes call `assertBillingAccess(req.user)`, which rejects users with the `member` role. Billing data is meant to be visible only to owners and admins. The new `/print` route skips that check, so any member of the org can fetch invoice amounts and periods by iterating ids. Add `assertBillingAccess(req.user)` as the first line of the handler, and add a test that a member gets 403.

findings.title: Amount is divided by 100 regardless of currency
findings.explanation: `src/lib/money.ts` says never to divide by 100 and to use its helpers, because JPY and KRW have 0 decimals and BHD and KWD have 3. A 5000 JPY invoice would print as 50.00 JPY, and a KWD invoice would be off by a factor of 10. This is a printed accounting document, so wrong amounts are a serious bug. Use `fromMinorUnits(Number(invoice.amount), invoice.currency).toFixed(minorUnitDigits(invoice.currency))`.

findings.title: Period dates are truncated in UTC
findings.explanation: `period_start` and `period_end` are TIMESTAMPTZ. Taking `toISOString().slice(0, 10)` gives the UTC date. If the period boundaries are not at UTC midnight, the printed dates can differ from what the web UI shows, because the UI uses local `toLocaleDateString`. An accounting copy should be unambiguous. Either state that the dates are UTC, or format in the org's timezone. Also consider whether `period_end` is exclusive, since it may show as the day after the last billed day.

findings.title: Status and currency are interpolated into HTML without escaping
findings.explanation: `org_name` is escaped, but `invoice.status` and `invoice.currency` are not. They are probably constrained values today, but a later change could make them free text and open an XSS hole. Escape every interpolated string, or use a small template helper that escapes by default.

findings.title: Sensitive HTML response has no cache or security headers
findings.explanation: The response contains financial data and has no `Cache-Control: private, no-store`. Shared proxies and browsers may cache it. Consider also setting a restrictive Content-Security-Policy and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. If a download is intended, set `Content-Disposition`. The markup also lacks `<html>`, `<meta charset>` and `<title>`, so non-ASCII org names may render wrongly. Add `<meta charset="utf-8">`.

findings.title: Invoice id is not validated
findings.explanation: `Number(req.params.invoiceId)` yields NaN for non-numeric input, which makes Postgres throw and returns a 500 instead of a 404 or 400. This matches the existing route, but it is better to validate with zod (`z.coerce.number().int().positive()`) and share the logic.

findings.title: No tests for the new endpoint
findings.explanation: Add tests for the cross-org 404, the member 403, the escaping of org names, and a zero-decimal currency such as JPY and a three-decimal one such as KWD. These would have caught both issues above.

Review this pull request. ## Add printable invoice download Customers want a printable copy of an invoice for their accounting team. Adds `GET /invoices/:invoiceId/print`, which returns a simple HTML invoice. Scoped to the caller's organization like the other invoice routes. ## Diff ```diff diff --git a/src/routes/invoices.ts b/src/routes/invoices.ts index 938fffd..04598f2 100644 --- a/src/routes/invoices.ts +++ b/src/routes/invoices.ts @@ -39,3 +39,25 @@ invoicesRouter.get('/:invoiceId', async (req, res) => { if (!rows[0]) return res.status(404).json({ error: 'not_found' }) res.json(serializeInvoice(rows[0])) }) + +invoicesRouter.get('/:invoiceId/print', async (req, res) => { + const { rows } = await pool.query( + `SELECT i.id, i.amount, i.currency, i.status, i.period_start, i.period_end, o.name AS org_name + FROM invoices i JOIN organizations o ON o.id = i.org_id + WHERE i.id = $1 AND i.org_id = $2`, + [Number(req.params.invoiceId), req.user.orgId], + ) + const invoice = rows[0] + if (!invoice) return res.status(404).json({ error: 'not_found' }) + const amount = (Number(invoice.amount) / 100).toFixed(2) + res.type('html').send(` +

Invoice #${invoice.id}

+

${escapeHtml(invoice.org_name)}

+

Period: ${invoice.period_start.toISOString().slice(0, 10)} to ${invoice.period_end.toISOString().slice(0, 10)}

+

Amount due: ${amount} ${invoice.currency.toUpperCase()}

+

Status: ${invoice.status}

`) +}) + +function escapeHtml(value: string): string { + return value.replace(/[&<>"']/g, (c) => ({ '&': '&', '<': '<', '>': '>', '"': '"', "'": ''' })[c] as string) +} ``` The repository is checked out at this pull request's head commit in the current directory. You can read any file in it with the Read, Grep, and Glob tools before answering. Before answering, check the change specifically for: authorization and tenant isolation; race conditions and concurrent requests; database migration safety on large tables and during rolling deploys; API changes that break existing clients; retries and idempotency of side effects such as payments; date and time handling; injection; sensitive data in logs; pagination and boundary conditions. Report every problem you would raise in a code review, from blocking issues to nits. Respond with only a JSON object, no prose before or after it: {"findings": [{"file": "path/to/file", "line": , "severity": "blocking" | "non-blocking" | "nit", "title": "", "explanation": ""}]} Use an empty findings list if you would approve the pull request as it is. Write the review in English.
